title: Credit Builder Accounts Due-Day Buffer After a Returned AutoPay Debit
content:
When AutoPay is turned on again on a Credit Builder account, a buffer of days is added to the account's current due day according to how the account's most recent AutoPay debit was returned and made good.

## Buffer for the returned debit

- When the account's most recent AutoPay debit (the latest payment made through the AutoPay channel; when two were posted on the same day, the one booked first counts as the latest) was returned in the 12 whole calendar months before today (a return line pointing at it dated today counts, and one dated on the same day of the month 12 months earlier falls outside them) and the borrower's own payment made it good within the late-fee grace period after that debit's due date (the payment looked at is the latest payment posted toward that due date, and when two were posted toward it on the same day the one booked first counts as the latest: it makes the debit good only when no return points at it, it is dated after the return and it is dated no more than the plan's late-fee grace days after the due date, counted as that payment's date less the due date; when a return points at that latest payment, the debit has not been made good), the buffer is those days plus one, so the new due day falls the day after the borrower's funds arrived.
- When that AutoPay debit was returned in those months but was made good only after the grace period, or has not been made good, the buffer is a flat 3 days.
- When it was not returned in those months, or the account has no AutoPay debit, there is no return buffer.

The plan's late-fee grace days are 15 on every Credit Builder Accounts plan. The AutoPay debit's due date is the installment due date on its payment entry; a return points at a payment when a returned-payment entry names that payment as the one it reverses.

| Most recent AutoPay debit | Latest payment toward its due date | Buffer |
|---|---|---|
| returned within the 12 months | dated after the return, not returned, at most 15 days after the due date | that payment's date less the due date, plus 1 day |
| returned within the 12 months | dated more than 15 days after the due date | 3 days |
| returned within the 12 months | a return points at it, or it is the debit itself | 3 days |
| not returned within the 12 months, or no AutoPay debit | not looked at | none |

## Worked dates (hypothetical)

Due date 5 March; the AutoPay debit for it returned 7 March; the borrower's payment toward 5 March posted 11 March and not returned: 6 days, buffer 7 days. Had that payment been posted 22 March (17 days): buffer 3 days.
